description:
On January 17, 2024, Deadra Johnson — a former Executive Director of the Killeen Housing Authority in Killeen, Texas, who held the position from January 10, 2019, until her resignation in August 2022 — was arrested by federal authorities after a grand jury indicted her on nine counts of embezzlement and one count of making false statements under 18 U.S.C. § 641 and 18 U.S.C. § 1001. Johnson pleaded guilty on February 11, 2025, to one count of theft of government property, and on November 18, 2025, U.S. District Judge David Counts sentenced her in Waco federal court to 37 months in federal prison, three years of supervised release, and $297,473.30 in restitution. During her tenure, Johnson fraudulently diverted HUD-funded Killeen Housing Authority accounts to pay her personal rent, utilities, auto maintenance, internet service, first-class airline tickets, furniture, and down payments on two personal vehicles, concealing the scheme through multiple kickback arrangements with KHA contractors and vendors. The original nine-count indictment charged just under $70,000 in documented losses, but the federal investigation's broader reconstruction of the fraud scope produced the $297,473.30 restitution figure — nearly four times the charged amount — reflecting conduct that spanned her entire tenure. The Killeen Housing Authority, which served hundreds of low-income and military families in Bell County through several hundred thousand dollars in annual HUD funding, became defunct following Johnson's resignation and the ensuing federal investigation, leaving residents without the housing assistance they had depended on.
